svg.title: RIEMANN F4 — The proof as literature: the 209 references of the blueprint on a timeline, which statements cite each, and what falls if one is wrong
svg.desc: The blueprint's reference list runs from Riemann's paper of 1859 to Alpöge's announcement of 2026, and 196 of its statements carry a source line citing one or more entries. This poster reads the proof as a history. The timeline puts every reference in its decade, a chip each, with the number of statements that cite it: the published and modified results the proof takes from it. The table ranks the references the proof leans on most, and gives each one's upward cone, every statement that rests on a statement citing it through the blueprint's uses edges, which is what would fall if the result were wrong; T1 and T2 descend from the top, this ascends from a leaf. The last card lists the references no statement cites. A citation here is the blueprint's attribution of a statement to a source, not a claim that the source proves it as stated. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

svg.text: A chip is one entry of the blueprint's reference list: the authors' surnames and the year, the title abridged, and the number of statements whose source line cites it. Chips stand in their decade, in order of year, and a decade's row says how many of its references are cited.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A title links to the paper, by its DOI where it has one, else a stable scan or its zbMATH record; the id beneath links to the blueprint's entry. The paper links are the diagram's own, not the blueprint's: looked up on Crossref and zbMATH and settled by hand where they disagreed (src/papers.toml).

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Cited by counts statements, not uses: a statement citing a reference is a published or modified result the blueprint attributes to it. 90 statements cite more than one source, and a few cite a section or lemma of one.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The upward cone of a reference is every statement that rests, through the uses edges, on a statement citing it: the statements citing it, their users, their users' users, up to the main theorems. Its size is a measure of how much of the proof stands on the result; whether the cone reaches a theorem of

svg.text: Not cited means no statement's source line names the reference. The blueprint lists it; the diagram cannot say why, and does not.

svg.text: 209 references from 1859 to 2026, in 14 decades; the fullest are the 1970s (39), the 1990s (38), the 1980s (31).

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 196 statements carry a source line: 140 published, 56 modified; 2 of them name no entry (classical, or a source the list does not hold).

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 174 references are cited, 327 citations in all; 35 are cited by no statement. Citations per reference: 101 cited 1 time, 34 cited 2 times, 20 cited 3 times, 12 cited 4 times, 3 cited 6 times, 1 cited 7

svg.text: Most cited bernstein-zelevinsky-1977 (9), faltings-chai-1990 (8), harish-chandra-1966 (8), tate-1963 (7), harish-chandra-1968 (6).

svg.text: 172 of the 174 cited references have a cone that reaches a theorem of Main.lean; the Riemann Hypothesis rests on all of them. The other 2: casselman-shalika-1980, shintani-1976.
